([[Montverde, Florida]]) | college = [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] (2021–2022) | highlights = * [[American Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|AAC Freshman of the Year]] (2022) * First-team All-[[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] (2022) * AAC All-Freshman Team (2022) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship|FIBA Americas U16 Championship]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship|2019 Brazil]]|[[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Jalen Montez Duren''' (born November 18, 2003) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]]. A [[Center (basketball)|center]], he stands {{convert|6|ft|11|in|m|2|abbr=}} and weighs {{convert|250|lbs|kg|0|}}. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruit|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2021 class. Duren was ranked as the top player in the 2022 class before reclassifying. ==Early life== Hailing from [[New Castle, Delaware]],{{cite news|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/adamzagoria/2019/05/11/if-the-nba-abandons-one-and-done-in-2022-remember-the-names-emoni-bates-and-jalen-duren/?sh=6177a021465a|title=If The NBA Abandons One-And-Done In 2022, Remember The Names Emoni Bates And Jalen Duren|work=[[Forbes]]|first=Adam|last=Zagoria|date=May 11, 2019|access-date=January 6, 2021}} Duren grew up playing football and baseball in addition to basketball, which he ended up focusing on as he grew older and improved his skills.{{cite news|url=https://www.news-press.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/12/21/getting-know-five-star-roman-catholic-sophomore-center-jalen-duren/2702148001/|title=Getting to know five-star Roman Catholic sophomore center Jalen Duren|work=[[The News-Press]]|first=Alex|last=Martin|date=December 21, 2019|access-date=January 6, 2021}} By the eighth grade he measured about {{Height|ft=6|in=8}}, gaining recognition on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) circuit playing with Team Final and winning the MADE Lea8ue title.{{cite news|url=https://www.madehoops.com/news_article/show/945393|title=MADE Hoops Alumni Series: The Rise Of Jalen Duren Began With The Winter Circuit|work=MADE Hoops|first=Eric|last=Hampford|date=August 30, 2018|access-date=January 6, 2021}} Strong showings at the MADE Hoops Middle School Academy and the CP3 Rising Stars Camp that summer solidified his position as one of the top players in his class.{{cite news|url=https://www.philadelphiasportsdigest.com/news_article/show/991381|title=Boys' Basketball: Jalen Duren Stands Tall as Roman Handles La Salle to Take First Place in Philadelphia Catholic League|work=Philadelphia Sports Digest|first=Rich|last=Flanagan|date=February 3, 2019|access-date=January 6, 2021}} ==High school career== Duren committed to playing high school basketball at [[Roman Catholic High School]] in [[Philadelphia|Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]] along with AAU teammate and highly-ranked guard Justice Williams. He averaged 12.8 [[Point (basketball)|points]], 9.3 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and 2.5 [[Block (basketball)|blocks]] per game while shooting 71 percent from the field as a freshman, leading his team to their second consecutive [[Philadelphia Catholic League]] title.{{cite news|url=https://phillysportsnetwork.com/2020/12/14/jalen-duren/|title=The recruitment of Philadelphia basketball phenom Jalen Duren|work=Philly Sports Network|first=Leader|last=Johnson|date=December 14, 2020|access-date=January 5, 2021}}{{cite news|url=https://catholicphilly.com/2019/03/news/sports/roman-catholic-takes-2nd-straight-cl-crown-4th-in-5-years/|title=Roman Catholic takes 2nd straight CL crown, 4th in 5 years|work=Catholic Philly|first=John|last=Knebels|date=March 1, 2019|access-date=January 6, 2021}} He earned first-team all-league and second-team all-state honors, and was named a [[MaxPreps]] Freshman All-American.{{cite news|url=https://aopathletics.org/news/2019/5/14/xx-2019-pa-sportswriters-boys-basketball-all-state-team.aspx?path=mbball|title=11 AOP Standouts Named To 2019 PA Sportswriters Boys' Basketball All-State Team|publisher=aopathletics.org|date=May 15, 2019|access-date=January 6, 2020}}{{cite news|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/OprYR7BMzk6w7vB7GJ-FmA/2018-19-maxpreps-boys-basketball-freshman-all-american-team.htm|title=2018-19 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Freshman All-American Team|work=[[MaxPreps]]|first=Jordan|last=Divens|date=April 19, 2019|access-date=January 6, 2020}} That summer he was a standout performer at the 2019 Nike Elite 100 Camp.{{cite news|url=https://247sports.com/ContentGallery/Emoni-Bates-Michigan-State-Chris-Livingston-Kentucky-Ohio-State-Jalen-Duren-Villanova-Jalen-Washington-Indiana-Purdue-133269470/#133269470_2|title=Nike Elite 100: Top 10 Class of 2022 Performers|work=[[247Sports]]|first=Brian|last=Snow|date=June 28, 2019|access-date=January 6, 2021}}{{cite news|url=http://www.burlisononbasketball.com/2019/06/ten-standouts-from-nike-elite-100-camp/|title=Ten standouts from Nike Elite 100 Camp|work=Burlison on Basketball|first=Frank|last=Burlison|date=June 26, 2019|access-date=January 6, 2021}} Duren averaged 18.1 points, 12.5 rebounds and 3.4 blocks per contest during his second year, leading his team to an 18–10 record.{{cite news|url=https://www.inquirer.com/high-school-sports/pennsylvania/jalen-duren-roman-catholic-montverde-transfer-20200414.html|title=Roman Catholic star Jalen Duren transfers to Montverde Academy in Florida|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|first=Phil|last=Anastasia|date=April 14, 2020|access-date=January 6, 2020}}{{cite news|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/gdEsVKDwjkarlc6uLBrfnA/maxpreps-2019-20-boys-basketball-sophomore-all-american-team.htm|title=MaxPreps 2019-20 Boys Basketball Sophomore All-American Team|work=[[MaxPreps]]|first=Jordan|last=Divens|date=April 1, 2020|access-date=January 6, 2020}} In the first round of the Catholic League playoffs he recorded 18 points and 18 rebounds against [[Bonner & Prendergast Catholic High School|Bonner-Prendergast]], hitting the game-winning [[buzzer beater]] in the 61–59 victory on [[Valentine's Day]].{{cite news|url=https://www.delcotimes.com/sports/roman-big-man-durens-buzzer-beating-putback-quiets-bonner-prendie/article_932e3de8-4fa5-11ea-ba67-730add6bd3e7.html|title=Roman big man Duren's buzzer-beating putback quiets Bonner-Prendie|work=[[Delaware County Daily Times]]|first=Jack|last=McCaffery|date=February 14, 2020|access-date=January 6, 2021}} He added 20 points and 18 rebounds in their 83–73 semi-final win over regular season champions [[Archbishop Wood Catholic High School|Archbishop Wood]] at the [[Palestra]].{{cite news|url=https://www.theintell.com/sports/20200219/roman-catholic-big-man-jalen-duren-too-tall-task-for-archbishop-wood|title=Roman Catholic, big man Jalen Duren too tall a task for Archbishop Wood|work=[[The Intelligencer (Doylestown, Pennsylvania)|The Intelligencer]]|first=Todd|last=Thorpe|date=February 19, 2020|access-date=January 6, 2021}} They were unable to defend their league crown, though, as they were defeated by [[Saints John Neumann and Maria Goretti Catholic High School|Neumann Goretti]] in the title game; Duren contributed 11 points and 16 rebounds in the 66–58 loss.{{cite news|url=https://fusion.inquirer.com/high-school-sports/pennsylvania/neumann-goretti-boys-basketball-roman-catholic-score-catholic-league-title-20200225.html|title=Neumann Goretti beats Roman Catholic for Catholic League boys' crown|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|first=Phil|last=Anastasia|date=February 24, 2020|access-date=January 6, 2020}} In the first round of the [[Pennsylvania Interscholastic Athletic Association|PIAA]] class 6A playoffs, they defeated [[Coatesville Area High School|Coatesville]] 81–75 with Duren posting 13 points and eight rebounds.{{cite news|url=https://rawsports.tv/wp/coatesville-falls-short-in-attempt-to-knock-off-roman-catholic-in-opening-round-of-6a-state-playoffs-by-tyler-harden/|title=Coatesville falls short in attempt to knock off Roman Catholic in opening round of 6A State Playoffs|work=Raw Sports|first=Tyler|last=Harden|date=March 8, 2020|access-date=January 6, 2020}} He recorded 20 points, six rebounds and eight blocks in their 62–51 quarter-final win over [[Pennridge School District|Pennridge]] before play was canceled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite news|url=https://papreplive.com/2020/03/12/durens-defense-helps-roman-catholic-overcome-pennridges-heart-in-state-playoffs/|title=Duren's defense helps Roman Catholic overcome Pennridge's heart in PIAA-6A 2nd round|work=PA Prep Live|first=Andrew|last=Robinson|date=March 12, 2020|access-date=January 6, 2020}} At the end of the year he collected first-team all-league, first-team all-state and MaxPreps Sophomore All-American honors.{{cite news|url=https://www.phillytrib.com/sports/basketball/all-catholic-league-boys-basketball-team-announced/article_9b5abf4c-f5d3-54a9-a5de-be5ac2cc9ef8.html|title=All-Catholic League boy's basketball team announced|work=[[The Philadelphia Tribune]]|first=Donald|last=Hunt|date=February 14, 2020|access-date=January 6, 2021}}{{cite news|url=https://fusion.inquirer.com/high-school-sports/pennsylvania/jalen-duren-roman-catholic-high-school-all-state-basketball-20200502.html|title=Sophomore center Jalen Duren among three Roman Catholic players selected to Class 6A all-state basketball teams|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|first=Phil|last=Anastasia|date=May 2, 2020|access-date=January 6, 2020}} For his junior year Duren transferred to [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]], who was in the process of joining the independent National Interscholastic Basketball Conference (NIBC) with other elite programs like [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill]], [[Wasatch Academy]] and Sunrise Christian amidst the COVID-19 pandemic.{{cite news|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/boys-basketball/os-sp-hs-mait-advance-0127-20210127-bgozywat4feqfbbtu5bwigg7hy-story.html|title=No. 1 Montverde basketball hosts 2 weekends of big games|work=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|first=Buddy|last=Collings|date=January 27, 2021|access-date=March 22, 2021}} Duren was one of only five underclassmen named to the [[Sports Illustrated]] Preseason All-American team.{{cite news|url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/jalen-duren-catches-shot-block-shots-montverde|title=Elite 2022 F Jalen Duren Prefers Catching Shots Over Swatting Them|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|first=Jason|last=Jordan|date=February 9, 2021|access-date=March 22, 2021}} In January 2021, Duren had a strong showing competing against high-level talent at the St. James NIBC Invitational in [[Washington, D.C.]],{{cite news|url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/jalen-duren-kennedy-chandler-stars-shine-at-st-james-nibc-invitational|title=Jalen Duren, Kennedy Chandler, Felix Okpara and Others Shine at the St. James NIBC Invitational|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|first=Jason|last=Jordan|date=January 11, 2021|access-date=March 22, 2021}}{{cite news|url=https://247sports.com/college/villanova/Article/The-St-James-NIBC-Invitational-Elite-big-man-Jalen-Duren-talks-shop-No-2-2022-recruiting-159485964/|title=The St. James NIBC Invitational: Elite big man Jalen Duren talks shop|work=[[247Sports]]|date=January 17, 2021|access-date=March 22, 2021}} including a [[SportsCenter]] Top 10 play against [[Wasatch Academy]] where he blocked a shot by catching the ball in mid-air. On March 11, Montverde avenged their only loss of the season by defeating Sunrise Christian 61–57 for the inaugural NIBC championship; Duren finished with 13 points and seven rebounds.{{cite news|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/aFsTcZ4LxEmIZY9nKE7wNw/high-school-basketball--no-1-montverde-academy-defeats-no-3-sunrise-christian-academy-61-57-to-win-inaugural-nibc-championship.htm|title=High school basketball: No. 1 Montverde Academy defeats No. 3 Sunrise Christian Academy 61-57 to win inaugural NIBC championship|work=[[MaxPreps]]|first=Jordan|last=Divens|date=March 12, 2021|access-date=March 22, 2021}} He averaged 15.5 points, 10.6 rebounds and 2.4 blocks per game in NIBC conference play, leading the Eagles to a 12–1 league record (20–1 overall).{{cite news|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/K4zTFklsnE6tRRppzkmMkA/jalen-duren-named-2020-21-maxpreps-florida-high-school-basketball-player-of-the-year.htm|title=Jalen Duren named 2020-21 MaxPreps Florida High School Basketball Player of the Year|work=[[MaxPreps]]|first=Jordan|last=Divens|date=March 11, 2021|access-date=March 22, 2021}} He was also recognized as the 2020–21 MaxPreps Florida High School Basketball Player of the Year. ===Recruiting=== Duren overtook [[Emoni Bates]] in his Junior Year as the top prospect in the 2022 recruiting class and was ranked one over Bates by [[ESPN]], [[247Sports]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]. On August 6, 2021, he reclassified to the 2021 class and committed to playing college basketball for [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] over offers from [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]], the [[NBA G League]] and the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|Australia NBL]].{{Cite web|last=Jackson|first=Wilton|title=Top Basketball Prospect Jalen Duren Commits to 19 points, grabbed 19 rebounds and blocked five shots in a 74–62 win against [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky]].{{cite news |title=Duren leads No. 11 Memphis past Western Kentucky 74-62 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401371916 |access-date=March 1, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 19, 2021}} He was named to the First Team All-[[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] as well as AAC Freshman of the Year.{{cite press release|url=https://theamerican.org/news/2022/3/8/american-athletic-conference-announces-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|title=American Athletic Conference Announces Men’s Basketball Honors|publisher=[[American Athletic Conference]] |date=March 9, 2022 |accessdate=March 9, 2022}} Duren lead Memphis to their first [[NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]] appearance since [[2014 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2014]] leading the Tigers to the round of 32.{{Cite web |last=Munz |first=Jason |title=Memphis basketball pushes Gonzaga to brink but falls short in NCAA Tournament |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2022/03/19/memphis-basketball-ncaa-tournament-run-ends-loss-gonzaga/7107955001/ |access-date=2022-04-18 |website=The Commercial Appeal |language=en-US}} As a freshman, he averaged 12 points, 8.1 rebounds and 2.1 blocks per game. On April 18, 2022, Duren declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{Cite web |date=2022-04-18 |title=Freshman Duren to leave Memphis for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33762796/jalen-duren-developing-lot-different-ways-one-season-memphis-men-basketball-program-enter-nba-draft |access-date=2022-04-18 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} ==National team career== Duren played for [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]] in [[Belém]], Brazil. He averaged 10.3 points, 8.2 rebounds and two blocks per game en route to a gold medal and a spot on the tournament all-star five team. ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}}
